questions.question: Which of the following substances regulates muscle actions?
questions.explanation_en: Calcium binds to troponin, causing tropomyosin to move and expose myosin-binding sites on actin.

questions.question: Which of the following substances acts at the neuromuscular junction to excite the muscle fibers of a motor unit?
questions.explanation_en: Acetylcholine is released by motor neurons at the neuromuscular junction to initiate muscle fiber depolarization.

questions.question: When throwing a baseball, an athlete’s arm is rapidly stretched just before throwing the ball. Which structure detects and responds to that stretch by reflexively increasing muscle activity?
questions.explanation_en: Muscle spindles detect changes in muscle length and trigger the stretch reflex to increase muscle activation.

questions.question: From which of the following is the heart’s electrical impulse normally initiated?
questions.explanation_en: The sinoatrial (SA) node serves as the heart’s natural pacemaker.

questions.question:
Which of the following occurs during the QRS complex of a typical ECG?

I. depolarization of the atrium
II. repolarization of the atrium
III. repolarization of the ventricle
IV. depolarization of the ventricle
questions.explanation_en: The QRS complex represents ventricular depolarization, while atrial repolarization occurs simultaneously but is masked by the larger ventricular signal.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the role of troponin in skeletal muscle contraction?
options: It binds to myosin and provides energy for cross-bridge cycling.
It blocks actin’s myosin-binding sites until calcium binds.
It stores calcium inside the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
It pumps calcium back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum to end contraction.
questions.answer_text: It blocks actin’s myosin-binding sites until calcium binds.
questions.explanation_en: Troponin is part of the regulatory complex; when calcium binds to troponin, tropomyosin shifts and exposes actin’s myosin-binding sites.

questions.question: Acetylcholine released at the neuromuscular junction primarily causes which of the following?
options: Opening of ligand-gated ion channels on the muscle membrane
Release of calcium from the sarcoplasmic reticulum directly
Inhibition of motor neuron firing via presynaptic blockade
Immediate detachment of myosin from actin
questions.answer_text: Opening of ligand-gated ion channels on the muscle membrane
questions.explanation_en: ACh binds receptors on the motor end plate, opening ligand-gated channels and initiating depolarization of the sarcolemma.

questions.question: The primary immediate energy source used by myosin ATPase during cross-bridge cycling is:
questions.explanation_en: Myosin ATPase directly hydrolyzes ATP to power cross-bridge cycling; other substrates support ATP resynthesis.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the function of the sarcoplasmic reticulum in skeletal muscle?
options: It provides structural support to the muscle fiber.
It stores and releases calcium to regulate contraction.
It generates action potentials along the muscle membrane.
It produces acetylcholine to excite the motor end plate.
questions.answer_text: It stores and releases calcium to regulate contraction.
questions.explanation_en: The sarcoplasmic reticulum stores calcium and releases it to initiate muscle contraction.

questions.question: Which of the following events occurs FIRST in the excitation–contraction coupling sequence?
options: Acetylcholine binds to receptors on the motor end plate.
Tropomyosin moves away from actin binding sites.
questions.answer_text: Acetylcholine binds to receptors on the motor end plate.
questions.explanation_en: ACh binding at the motor end plate is the earliest event that initiates muscle fiber depolarization.

questions.question: The Golgi tendon organ is MOST closely associated with detecting changes in:
questions.explanation_en: Golgi tendon organs detect changes in muscle tension and help protect against excessive force.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes extrafusal muscle fibers?
options: They are the primary force-producing fibers in skeletal muscle.
They detect muscle stretch and initiate the stretch reflex.
They are sensory neurons located within the tendon.
They generate the heart’s electrical impulses.
questions.answer_text: They are the primary force-producing fibers in skeletal muscle.
questions.explanation_en: Extrafusal fibers are the main contractile fibers responsible for producing force.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the function of the SA node?
options: It delays electrical conduction to allow ventricular filling.
It initiates the heart’s electrical impulse as the primary pacemaker.
It transmits impulses directly to the ventricles.
It inhibits sympathetic nervous system activity.
questions.answer_text: It initiates the heart’s electrical impulse as the primary pacemaker.
questions.explanation_en: The SA node initiates the heart’s electrical impulse under normal conditions.

questions.question: During a typical ECG, the P wave represents:
questions.explanation_en: The P wave corresponds to atrial depolarization.

questions.question: Which of the following is MOST associated with ventricular repolarization on a typical ECG?
questions.explanation_en: The T wave represents ventricular repolarization.

questions.question: A motor unit is best defined as:
options: a muscle fiber and all sensory neurons that detect stretch
a motor neuron and all the muscle fibers it innervates
all the muscles that cross a joint
a group of tendons attaching muscle to bone
questions.answer_text: a motor neuron and all the muscle fibers it innervates
questions.explanation_en: A motor unit consists of a motor neuron and all the muscle fibers it innervates.

questions.question: Which of the following would MOST directly increase the speed of a stretch reflex response?
options: Greater activation of muscle spindles due to rapid stretch
Greater activation of Golgi tendon organs
questions.answer_text: Greater activation of muscle spindles due to rapid stretch
questions.explanation_en: Muscle spindles respond strongly to rapid lengthening, accelerating the stretch reflex.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly represents the heart’s normal electrical conduction pathway?
options: AV node → SA node → Purkinje fibers
SA node → AV node → Bundle of His → Purkinje fibers
Purkinje fibers → AV node → SA node
SA node → Purkinje fibers → AV node
questions.answer_text: SA node → AV node → Bundle of His → Purkinje fibers
questions.explanation_en: Normal conduction proceeds SA node → AV node → Bundle of His → Purkinje fibers.

questions.question: If calcium does NOT bind to troponin during attempted contraction, which of the following will occur?
options: Myosin heads bind more strongly to actin.
questions.explanation_en: Without calcium binding to troponin, tropomyosin remains in place, preventing cross-bridge formation.

questions.question: Which statement about the QRS complex is MOST accurate?
questions.explanation_en: The QRS complex corresponds primarily to ventricular depolarization.

questions.question: Which of the following is the definition of power?
questions.explanation_en: Power is defined as the rate of doing work and can be expressed as force multiplied by velocity.

questions.question: To compare performances of Olympic weightlifters of different body weights, the classic formula divides the load lifted by the athlete’s:
options: body weight to the two-thirds power
questions.answer_text: body weight to the two-thirds power
questions.explanation_en: Relative strength is commonly calculated by dividing the load lifted by body weight to the two-thirds power.

questions.question:
During a free weight exercise, muscle force varies with which of the following?

I. perpendicular distance from the weight to the body joint
II. joint angle
III. movement acceleration
IV. movement velocity squared
questions.explanation_en: Muscle force during free weight exercise depends on moment arm length, joint angle, and acceleration. Velocity squared applies to fluid resistance, not free weights.

questions.question: A vertical jump involves knee, hip, and shoulder movement primarily in which of the following anatomical planes?
questions.explanation_en: Flexion and extension movements occur primarily in the sagittal plane.

questions.question:
An athlete is performing a concentric isokinetic elbow flexion and extension exercise. Which type(s) of levers occur(s) at the elbow during this exercise?

I. first class
II. second class
III. third class
questions.explanation_en: Elbow flexion and extension function as third-class levers, where muscle force is applied between the axis and resistance.

questions.question: Work is BEST defined as:
questions.explanation_en: Work equals force applied through a displacement in the direction of the force.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes torque?
options: Force applied parallel to a lever arm
Rotary effect of a force acting about an axis
questions.answer_text: Rotary effect of a force acting about an axis
questions.explanation_en: Torque is the rotary effect of a force acting at a distance from a joint or axis.

questions.question: Increasing the perpendicular distance between a resistance and a joint axis will:
questions.explanation_en: Torque increases as the moment arm (perpendicular distance) increases.

questions.question: Which lever system provides the greatest mechanical advantage?
questions.explanation_en: Second-class levers place the resistance between the axis and force, maximizing mechanical advantage.

questions.question: Most human musculoskeletal movements operate as:
questions.explanation_en: Most human joints function as third-class levers, favoring speed and range of motion over force.

questions.question: Which anatomical plane divides the body into left and right halves?
questions.explanation_en: The sagittal plane divides the body into left and right portions.

questions.question: A lateral raise exercise primarily involves movement in which anatomical plane?
questions.explanation_en: Shoulder abduction during a lateral raise occurs in the frontal plane.

questions.question: Angular displacement refers to:
options: distance traveled by the center of mass
questions.explanation_en: Angular displacement is the change in joint angle during movement.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST explains why third-class levers are common in the human body?
options: They increase movement speed and range of motion
questions.answer_text: They increase movement speed and range of motion
questions.explanation_en: Third-class levers sacrifice force for increased speed and range of motion, which benefits athletic movement.

questions.question: Which variable directly determines linear acceleration according to Newton’s second law?
questions.explanation_en: Acceleration is directly proportional to the net force applied.

questions.question: During a squat, the greatest external torque at the knee occurs when:
options: the barbell is directly over the joint
questions.explanation_en: Torque is greatest when the perpendicular distance between the load and the joint axis is longest.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes center of mass?
options: Point at which mass is evenly distributed
questions.answer_text: Point at which mass is evenly distributed
questions.explanation_en: The center of mass is the point where the body's mass is evenly distributed in all directions.

questions.question: Which biomechanical principle explains why a wider base of support improves balance?
options: Lower center of mass relative to base of support
questions.answer_text: Lower center of mass relative to base of support
questions.explanation_en: A wider base of support increases stability by allowing the center of mass to remain within the base more easily.

questions.question: Which quantity is conserved in the absence of external forces?
questions.explanation_en: Momentum is conserved when no external forces act on a system.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST explains why increasing load reduces movement velocity during resistance exercise?
options: Greater mass requires greater force to accelerate
questions.answer_text: Greater mass requires greater force to accelerate
questions.explanation_en: As load increases, more force is required to accelerate it, typically reducing movement velocity.

questions.question: Which of the following substances can be metabolized anaerobically?
questions.explanation_en: Only glucose can be metabolized anaerobically via glycolysis.

questions.question: Which of the following reactions is the primary cause of metabolic acidosis (i.e., the decrease in intramuscular pH during high-intensity, fatiguing exercise)?
questions.explanation_en: ATP hydrolysis releases hydrogen ions, which directly lower muscle pH.

questions.question: Which of the following energy systems produces ATP at the quickest rate?
questions.explanation_en: The phosphagen system produces ATP at the fastest rate but has very limited capacity.

questions.question: Approximately how many net ATP are produced via the oxidative energy system from the metabolism of one glucose molecule?
questions.explanation_en: Modern estimates place ATP yield from one glucose molecule at approximately 30–34 ATP.

questions.question: Which of the following energy substrates cannot be depleted during extreme exercise intensities or durations?
questions.explanation_en: ATP concentration is tightly regulated and cannot be fully depleted without cell death.

questions.question: After a bout of resistance training, acute hormonal secretions provide all of the following information to the body EXCEPT
questions.explanation_en: Acute hormonal responses reflect stress magnitude, stress type, and metabolic demands, but they do not directly quantify total energy expended.

questions.question:
Which of the following hormones enhance(s) muscle tissue growth?

I. growth hormone
II. cortisol
III. IGF-I
IV. progesterone
questions.explanation_en: Growth hormone and IGF-I support anabolic processes related to muscle growth. Cortisol is catabolic, and progesterone is not a primary driver of hypertrophy.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of growth hormone?
questions.explanation_en: Growth hormone increases collagen synthesis, supporting connective tissue integrity. It also increases lipolysis, increases amino acid transport, and decreases glucose utilization.

questions.question: Which of the following hormones has the greatest influence on neural changes?
questions.explanation_en: Testosterone has the strongest association with neural adaptations related to strength, such as motor unit recruitment and neuromuscular efficiency.

questions.question: What type of resistance training workout promotes the highest growth hormone increases following the exercise session?
questions.explanation_en: Growth hormone responses are greatest with short rest intervals, high training volume, and high metabolic stress.

questions.question: Prolonged exposure to elevated hormone concentrations most commonly results in which cellular adaptation?
questions.explanation_en: Chronic exposure to high hormone levels leads to downregulation, reducing receptor number and cellular sensitivity.

questions.question: Which hormone type exerts its effects primarily by binding to intracellular receptors and directly influencing gene transcription?
questions.explanation_en: Steroid hormones are lipid-soluble, cross the cell membrane, and bind intracellular receptors to directly affect gene transcription.

questions.question: Which of the following hormones relies on a second-messenger system to exert its effects?
questions.explanation_en: Growth hormone is a peptide hormone that binds membrane receptors and signals via second-messenger pathways.

questions.question: Which regulatory mechanism helps maintain hormonal homeostasis by reducing hormone secretion once adequate levels are reached?
questions.explanation_en: Negative feedback loops inhibit further hormone secretion once sufficient physiological effects have been achieved.

questions.question: An athlete experiencing chronically elevated cortisol levels is MOST likely to experience which outcome?
questions.explanation_en: Cortisol is a catabolic hormone that promotes protein breakdown and suppresses immune function during prolonged stress.

questions.question: Which training variable manipulation is MOST associated with an acute anabolic hormonal environment?
options: long rest intervals with low volume
short rest intervals with high volume
questions.answer_text: short rest intervals with high volume
questions.explanation_en: Short rest intervals combined with high volume increase metabolic stress and are associated with acute anabolic hormonal responses.

questions.question: Which of the following adaptations occurs FIRST during the initial weeks of a resistance training program?
questions.explanation_en: Early strength gains are primarily due to neural adaptations such as increased motor unit recruitment and firing frequency rather than hypertrophy.

questions.question: Which resistance training adaptation is MOST responsible for improvements in rate of force development?
questions.explanation_en: Rate of force development is largely influenced by neural factors, particularly the speed and frequency of motor unit activation.

questions.question: Which of the following training variables is MOST critical for maximizing neural adaptations in anaerobic resistance training?
options: high volume with short rest intervals
heavy loads with long rest intervals
questions.answer_text: heavy loads with long rest intervals
questions.explanation_en: Neural adaptations are maximized by high-intensity loads (≥85% 1RM) with sufficient rest to maintain force output.

questions.question: Which adaptation contributes MOST to increased force transmission following chronic resistance training?
questions.explanation_en: Increased tendon stiffness improves the transmission of muscular force to the skeletal system, enhancing strength and power output.

questions.question: Which of the following changes is MOST characteristic of functional overreaching (FOR)?
options: short-term performance decrease followed by supercompensation
questions.answer_text: short-term performance decrease followed by supercompensation
questions.explanation_en: Functional overreaching involves a temporary decrease in performance that is followed by improvement after adequate recovery.

questions.question: Which resistance training adaptation is MOST reversible during periods of detraining?
questions.explanation_en: Muscle hypertrophy is lost more rapidly during detraining compared to neural or skeletal adaptations.

questions.question: A 17-year-old high school cross-country runner has been training aerobically for six months. Which muscular adaptation will most likely occur?
options: transformation from Type I to Type II fibers
questions.explanation_en: Aerobic training promotes hypertrophy and oxidative adaptations in Type I muscle fibers.

questions.question: The amount of blood ejected from the left ventricle during each beat is the:
questions.explanation_en: Stroke volume is the amount of blood ejected per beat.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT normally increase during an aerobic exercise session?
questions.explanation_en: Diastolic blood pressure typically remains unchanged or may slightly decrease during aerobic exercise.

questions.question: Mean arterial pressure is defined as the:
options: average blood pressure throughout the cardiac cycle
average of systolic and diastolic blood pressures
average systolic blood pressure during exercise
average of blood pressure and heart rate
questions.answer_text: average blood pressure throughout the cardiac cycle
questions.explanation_en: Mean arterial pressure reflects average arterial pressure across the cardiac cycle.

questions.question:
Primary training adaptations of elite aerobically trained athletes include which of the following?

I. increased maximal oxygen uptake
II. decreased blood lactate concentration
III. increased running economy
IV. decreased capillary density
questions.explanation_en: Aerobic training increases VO₂max, improves lactate handling, and enhances economy while increasing capillary density.

questions.question: Which adaptation is considered a PRIMARY peripheral adaptation to aerobic endurance training?
questions.explanation_en: Peripheral adaptations include increased mitochondrial density, capillarization, and oxidative enzyme activity within skeletal muscle.

questions.question: Which factor contributes MOST to increases in VO₂max following aerobic endurance training?
questions.explanation_en: Increases in VO₂max are driven largely by increases in stroke volume and blood volume, which enhance oxygen delivery.

questions.question: Which adaptation BEST explains improved exercise economy following aerobic training?
questions.explanation_en: Improved economy reflects reduced energy cost at a given workload due to enhanced neuromuscular coordination and efficiency.

questions.question: Which cardiovascular variable typically plateaus FIRST during progressive aerobic training?
questions.explanation_en: Stroke volume adaptations tend to plateau earlier, after which improvements rely more on peripheral adaptations.

questions.question: Which of the following adaptations is MOST specific to long-duration aerobic endurance training?
options: increased Type IIx fiber cross-sectional area
questions.explanation_en: Long-duration aerobic training increases capillary density to enhance oxygen delivery and waste removal.

questions.question: An 8-year-old boy dramatically increased his upper body strength after following a six-month resistance training program. Which of the following is MOST likely responsible for this gain?
questions.explanation_en: Strength gains in prepubescent children are primarily due to neural adaptations rather than hypertrophy.

questions.question: Growth cartilage in children is located at all of the following EXCEPT the:
questions.explanation_en: The diaphysis is the shaft of the bone and does not contain growth cartilage.

questions.question: The condition characterized by a bone mineral density more than 2.5 standard deviations below the young adult mean is called:
questions.explanation_en: Osteoporosis is defined as bone mineral density more than 2.5 SD below the young adult mean.

questions.question: Which of the following should be evaluated FIRST when designing a training program for a 68-year-old competitive female tennis player?
questions.explanation_en: Medical history must be assessed first to ensure safety before training older adults.

questions.question: Deconditioned female college athletes who participate in sports such as basketball and soccer appear to be at increased risk for developing injuries to the:
questions.explanation_en: Female athletes are at higher risk of knee injuries, particularly ACL injuries, especially when deconditioned.

questions.question: An Olympic weightlifter attempting a personal record is able to ignore the audience and concentrate solely on performance. Which ability is most likely being used?
questions.explanation_en: Selective attention allows athletes to focus on relevant cues while ignoring distractions.

questions.question: An athlete’s desire to perform to his or her potential is an example of:
questions.explanation_en: Achievement motivation reflects the drive to achieve success and reach potential.

questions.question: For a high school American football team, if any player squats two times his body weight, his name is placed on the wall. This is an example of:
questions.explanation_en: Adding recognition to reinforce behavior is positive reinforcement.

questions.question: How does an athlete’s optimal level of arousal change with limited skill and ability to perform the activity?
options: It is not related to the activity.
questions.explanation_en: Less-skilled athletes perform best at lower levels of arousal.

questions.question: In teaching the push press, which is an example of segmentation with pure-part training integration?
options: Practice the push press unloaded, progress to PVC pipe, then an unloaded bar.
Practice the dip, then dip with drive, then the entire push press.
Practice the dip, drive, and catch independently before the entire push press.
Practice dip and drive independently, then dip with drive, then catch, and finally the full push press.
questions.answer_text: Practice dip and drive independently, then dip with drive, then catch, and finally the full push press.
questions.explanation_en: Pure-part segmentation trains individual components separately before progressive integration into the full movement.

questions.question: Maintaining adequate glycogen stores:
options: spares the use of protein for energy
questions.answer_text: spares the use of protein for energy
questions.explanation_en: Adequate glycogen helps meet energy demands so the body relies less on amino acids (protein) for fuel.

questions.question: The following is the most likely contributor to fatigue and poor performance:
questions.explanation_en: Iron deficiency can reduce hemoglobin and oxygen delivery, commonly causing fatigue and reduced performance.

questions.question: Which of the following is a recommendation for lowering undesirably high levels of blood lipids?
options: limit saturated fatty acid intake to 30% of total calories
consume a minimum of 500 mg of dietary cholesterol per day
replace saturated fatty acids with monounsaturated or polyunsaturated fatty acids
questions.answer_text: replace saturated fatty acids with monounsaturated or polyunsaturated fatty acids
questions.explanation_en: Replacing saturated fats with unsaturated fats (mono/poly) is a common strategy to improve blood lipid profiles.

questions.question: Which of the following protein sources does not contain all essential amino acids in appreciable quantities?
questions.explanation_en: Many plant proteins (like lentils) are incomplete, meaning one or more essential amino acids are present in lower amounts.

questions.question: The primary macronutrient that is addressed in the precompetition meal is
questions.explanation_en: Precompetition meals emphasize carbohydrates to top off glycogen and support high-intensity performance.

questions.question: Which of the following makes the GREATEST contribution to total energy expenditure?
questions.explanation_en: Resting metabolic rate is typically the largest component of daily total energy expenditure for most people.

questions.question: Which of the following is characteristic of anorexia nervosa?
questions.explanation_en: A common feature is an intense preoccupation with food, body weight, and control of eating; normal body weight is not typical.

questions.question: When an eating disorder is suspected, the strength and conditioning professional should
options: monitor the athlete’s daily food intake
encourage further assessment by an eating disorder specialist
questions.answer_text: encourage further assessment by an eating disorder specialist
questions.explanation_en: The appropriate step is referral/encouraging assessment by a qualified specialist; monitoring intake or weigh-ins can worsen the situation.

questions.question: Which of the following dietary supplements is (are) considered a stimulant?
questions.explanation_en: Caffeine and citrus aurantium are stimulants; creatine and HMB are not.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of caffeine’s role in improving athletic performance?
questions.explanation_en: Caffeine does not decrease urine production; it may have mild diuretic effects, especially in non-habituated users.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST reason for aerobic endurance athletes to avoid erythropoietin use?
options: Hematocrit and hemoglobin levels may decrease
It may cause an unregulated increase in red blood cell production
Resistance to infectious disease may be impaired
It may reduce the ability of the blood to carry oxygen
questions.answer_text: It may cause an unregulated increase in red blood cell production
questions.explanation_en: Erythropoietin can dangerously increase red blood cell mass, raising blood viscosity and cardiovascular risk.

questions.question: Creatine supplementation improves all of the following variables EXCEPT
questions.explanation_en: Creatine primarily improves strength, power, and lean mass, but not aerobic endurance performance.

questions.question: Which of the following performance-enhancing substances is most likely to increase lean body mass?
questions.explanation_en: Anabolic steroids directly stimulate muscle protein synthesis and increase lean body mass.

questions.question: A college basketball coach would like to know which one of her players has the most muscular power. Which of the following is the MOST valid test for measuring muscular power?
questions.explanation_en: The vertical jump directly measures explosive lower-body power, making it the most valid test of muscular power.

questions.question:
When measuring maximal strength of a soccer player, which of the following could potentially adversely affect the test–retest reliability of the results?

I. using multiple testers
II. retesting at a different time of day
III. an athlete’s inexperience with the tested exercise
IV. using an established testing protocol
questions.explanation_en: Multiple testers, different testing times, and athlete inexperience can all reduce test–retest reliability; established protocols improve reliability.

questions.question: All of the following procedures should be followed when testing an athlete’s cardiovascular fitness in the heat EXCEPT
options: performing the test in an indoor facility
using salt tablets to retain water
scheduling the test in the morning
questions.answer_text: using salt tablets to retain water
questions.explanation_en: Salt tablets are not recommended during testing due to the risk of electrolyte imbalance.

questions.question: The bench press, vertical jump, and 10 m (11-yard) sprint are the MOST valid tests for which of the following American football positions?
questions.explanation_en: These tests assess strength, power, and short-distance acceleration—key performance qualities for defensive linemen.

questions.question: Which of the following sequences will produce the MOST reliable results?
options: 1RM power clean, T-test, 1.5 mile (2.4 km) run, 1RM bench press
T-test, 1RM power clean, 1RM bench press, 1.5 mile (2.4 km) run
1.5 mile (2.4 km) run, 1RM bench press, T-test, 1RM power clean
1RM bench press, 1RM power clean, T-test, 1.5 mile (2.4 km) run
questions.answer_text: T-test, 1RM power clean, 1RM bench press, 1.5 mile (2.4 km) run
questions.explanation_en: Testing should proceed from least fatiguing to most fatiguing to maximize reliability.

questions.question: Which of the following tests is MOST appropriate for assessing lower-body power in a large group setting with limited equipment?
questions.explanation_en: The vertical jump is valid, time-efficient, and requires minimal equipment, making it ideal for large groups.

questions.question: A strength coach wants to ensure high objectivity during testing. Which of the following practices BEST supports this goal?
options: using the same tester for all athletes
adjusting protocols based on athlete preference
questions.answer_text: using the same tester for all athletes
questions.explanation_en: Objectivity is maximized when the same tester administers and scores all tests using standardized procedures.

questions.question: Which of the following factors MOST directly affects the validity of a test?
options: whether the test measures the intended physical quality
the familiarity of the athlete with the test
questions.answer_text: whether the test measures the intended physical quality
questions.explanation_en: Validity refers to how well a test measures what it is intended to measure.

questions.question: For the following scenario, select the MOST appropriate test: Assessing maximal lower-body strength
questions.explanation_en: Test selection must align with the specific physical quality being assessed; the same test battery is not valid for all goals.

questions.question: For the following scenario, select the MOST appropriate test: Assessing lower-body explosive power
questions.explanation_en: Test selection must align with the specific physical quality being assessed; the same test battery is not valid for all goals.

questions.question: For the following scenario, select the MOST appropriate test: Assessing change-of-direction ability
questions.explanation_en: Test selection must align with the specific physical quality being assessed; the same test battery is not valid for all goals.

questions.question: For the following scenario, select the MOST appropriate test: Assessing intermittent aerobic capacity
questions.explanation_en: Test selection must align with the specific physical quality being assessed; the same test battery is not valid for all goals.

questions.question: For the following scenario, select the MOST appropriate testing approach: Untrained adolescent athletes
questions.explanation_en: Appropriate test selection depends on training status, safety, resources, and required measurement precision.

questions.question: For the following scenario, select the MOST appropriate testing approach: Elite powerlifters
questions.explanation_en: Appropriate test selection depends on training status, safety, resources, and required measurement precision.

questions.question: For the following scenario, select the MOST appropriate testing approach: Large team with limited time and equipment
questions.explanation_en: Appropriate test selection depends on training status, safety, resources, and required measurement precision.

questions.question: For the following scenario, select the MOST appropriate testing approach: Research setting requiring high precision
questions.explanation_en: Appropriate test selection depends on training status, safety, resources, and required measurement precision.

questions.question: Anaerobic capacity is quantified as the maximal power output achieved during activity lasting
questions.explanation_en: Anaerobic capacity reflects the ability to sustain high power primarily via glycolytic pathways, typically over ~30–90 seconds.

questions.question: Which of the following tests is NOT used to measure maximum muscular power?
questions.explanation_en: A 40-yard sprint is primarily a measure of speed/acceleration; the others are used as muscular power assessments.

questions.question:
Flexibility of which of these muscle groups or body areas is assessed during the sit-and-reach test?

I. hamstrings
II. erector spinae
III. lumbar spine
IV. hip flexors
questions.explanation_en: The sit-and-reach is intended to assess hamstring and lower-back (lumbar/erector spinae) flexibility.

questions.question: Which of the following is a reason for a trial of the T-test to be disqualified (see figure 13.11)?
options: touching the base of cone D
shuffling from cone C to cone D
crossing the feet from cone B to cone C
running forward from cone A to cone B
questions.answer_text: crossing the feet from cone B to cone C
questions.explanation_en: In the T-test, athletes must shuffle laterally without crossing the feet; crossing the feet is a disqualification.

questions.question: When compiling results from the volleyball team’s vertical jump testing, the strength and conditioning professional notices that most scores are similar, but there are three scores that are much higher than the rest. Which of the following measures of central tendency is most appropriate for this group?
questions.explanation_en: With extreme high outliers, the median best represents central tendency because it is resistant to outliers.

questions.question: Which of the following statistical measures BEST describes the spread or dispersion of test scores around the mean?
questions.explanation_en: Standard deviation quantifies how much individual scores vary from the mean.

questions.question: An athlete scores in the 90th percentile on a strength test. This indicates that the athlete performed better than
questions.explanation_en: A 90th percentile rank means the athlete outperformed 90% of the reference population.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST explains why normative data are important when interpreting test results?
options: They eliminate the need for repeated testing
They allow comparison to a reference population
They improve the validity of the test
questions.answer_text: They allow comparison to a reference population
questions.explanation_en: Normative data provide context by allowing an athlete’s performance to be compared to a relevant population.

questions.question: For the following scenario, select the MOST appropriate interpretation: An athlete scores in the 85th percentile on a power test
options: result is unreliable due to testing error
questions.explanation_en: Percentile ranks indicate relative performance, while large score variability suggests poor reliability.

questions.question: For the following scenario, select the MOST appropriate interpretation: An athlete scores near the 50th percentile on a strength test

questions.explanation_en: Mirrors should be placed at least 20 inches above the floor for safety.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key consideration when determining the space requirements of a college strength and conditioning facility?

number of athletic teams desiring to use the facility

questions.explanation_en: A minimum of 3 feet is recommended to allow adequate space for spotters.

questions.question: What is the recommended coach-to-participant ratio during peak weight room usage time in a collegiate setting?
questions.explanation_en: A 1:20 coach-to-participant ratio is recommended during peak collegiate weight room usage.

questions.explanation_en: Medical clearance to participate is provided by the certified athletic trainer.

questions.explanation_en: Finance and appraisal are not core competency domains for strength and conditioning professionals.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of an emergency plan?
questions.explanation_en: Emergency plans include communication, equipment, and personnel, but not emergency medicine.

questions.question: The axial skeleton includes the:

questions.question: The primary muscle group responsible for knee extension during a squat is the:
questions.explanation_en: The quadriceps are the primary movers during knee extension, which occurs when standing up from the bottom of a squat.

questions.question: Alveoli are responsible for:
options: Exchanging gases between air and blood
questions.answer_text: Exchanging gases between air and blood
questions.explanation_en: Alveoli are tiny air sacs in the lungs where the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide occurs between the lungs and the bloodstream.

questions.question: In a first-class lever (e.g., a seesaw), the fulcrum is positioned:
options: Between the load and the effort
Between the effort and the load
At the end of the lever arm
questions.answer_text: Between the load and the effort
questions.explanation_en: In a first-class lever, the fulcrum is positioned between the effort and the load.

questions.question: Which type of muscle action occurs when lowering a dumbbell during a curl?
questions.explanation_en: Eccentric muscle actions occur when the muscle lengthens under tension, such as when lowering a dumbbell during a curl.

questions.question: Using the torque equation (Torque = Force × Distance), which option produces the greatest torque?
questions.explanation_en: Torque = Force × Distance. 25 × 0.06 = 1.5 N·m, which is the highest torque among the options.

questions.question: Which energy system provides immediate energy for short, high-intensity activities (e.g., a 100-meter sprint)?
questions.explanation_en: The phosphagen system provides immediate energy for short, high-intensity activities like a 100-meter sprint.

questions.question: Which hormone helps maintain blood glucose levels during prolonged exercise by promoting glycogen breakdown in the liver?
questions.explanation_en: Glucagon is secreted to maintain blood glucose levels during prolonged exercise by promoting glycogen breakdown in the liver.

questions.question: High-intensity interval training (HIIT) is most associated with:
questions.explanation_en: HIIT causes a significant oxygen deficit during exercise, leading to greater oxygen debt afterward for recovery.

questions.question: Type I muscle fibers are best described as:
questions.explanation_en: Type I fibers are slow-twitch fibers that are highly fatigue-resistant and primarily rely on the aerobic energy system.

questions.question: The functional unit of a myofibril where muscle contraction occurs is the:
questions.explanation_en: The sarcomere is the structural and functional unit of a myofibril, where muscle contraction occurs.

questions.question: Calcium ions bind to which protein to initiate muscle contraction?
questions.explanation_en: Calcium ions bind to troponin, which triggers the conformational change that allows actin and myosin interaction for contraction.

questions.question: Which receptor detects changes in muscle length and triggers a stretch reflex?
questions.explanation_en: Muscle spindles detect changes in muscle length and initiate the stretch reflex to resist overstretching.

questions.question: Which part of a neuron conducts electrical impulses away from the cell body?
questions.explanation_en: Axons conduct electrical impulses away from the neuron’s cell body toward other neurons, muscles, or glands.

questions.question: Which neurotransmitter is released at the neuromuscular junction to initiate muscle contraction?
questions.explanation_en: Acetylcholine is the neurotransmitter that binds to receptors on muscle cells to initiate contraction.

questions.question: During high-intensity exercise, the preferred energy source for ATP production is typically:
questions.explanation_en: Carbohydrates are the preferred energy source during high-intensity exercise due to their efficiency in ATP production.

questions.question: Which vitamin is fat-soluble and commonly requires dietary fat for absorption?
questions.explanation_en: Vitamins A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble, meaning they are stored in body fat and require fat for absorption.

questions.question: Iron is a critical component of hemoglobin and primarily supports:
questions.explanation_en: Iron is a critical component of hemoglobin, responsible for carrying oxygen in the blood.

questions.question: A carbohydrate-loading strategy for endurance events typically involves:
options: Consuming a high-fat diet 1 day prior
Consuming a high-carbohydrate diet 3–7 days prior
questions.answer_text: Consuming a high-carbohydrate diet 3–7 days prior
questions.explanation_en: Carbohydrate loading involves increasing glycogen stores by consuming a high-carbohydrate diet days before an event.

questions.question: Recommended daily protein intake for athletes to support muscle repair and recovery is approximately:
questions.explanation_en: Athletes typically require 1.2–2.0 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight to support muscle repair and recovery.

questions.question: Endurance athletes are most likely to rely heavily on carbohydrates, such as:
questions.explanation_en: Endurance athletes, such as marathon runners, rely heavily on carbohydrates to fuel prolonged training sessions.

questions.question: Which supplement is best known for improving ATP resynthesis during short-duration, high-intensity exercise?
questions.explanation_en: Creatine improves ATP resynthesis during high-intensity, short-duration exercises such as sprinting and lifting.

questions.question: Which substance is banned due to its performance-enhancing and potential health-risk properties?
questions.explanation_en: Ephedrine is a banned substance due to its performance-enhancing and potential health-risk properties.

questions.question: Which supplement increases muscle carnosine levels and may delay fatigue by buffering hydrogen ions?
questions.explanation_en: Beta-alanine supplementation increases muscle carnosine levels, enhancing the ability to buffer hydrogen ions and delay fatigue.

questions.question: Which mineral is vital for nerve function and muscle contraction, and imbalances can contribute to cramps?
questions.explanation_en: Potassium is vital for nerve function and muscle contraction; imbalances can lead to cramps and weakness.

questions.question: Which method is a simple and effective way to assess hydration status in athletes?
questions.explanation_en: Urine color is a simple and effective method to assess hydration status—pale yellow indicates good hydration.

questions.question: Losing more than 2% of body weight through sweat can impair thermoregulation and increase risk of:
questions.explanation_en: Losing more than 2% of body weight through sweat can impair thermoregulation and increase the risk of heat-related illnesses like heatstroke.

questions.question: Carbohydrate consumption within what time frame post-exercise helps maximize glycogen resynthesis?
questions.explanation_en: Carbohydrate consumption within 30 minutes post-exercise maximizes glycogen resynthesis for better recovery.

questions.question: Which pre-competition meal is generally recommended to provide sustained energy without GI discomfort?
options: Moderate carbohydrate, low-fat, moderate protein meal
questions.answer_text: Moderate carbohydrate, low-fat, moderate protein meal
questions.explanation_en: A balanced pre-competition meal with moderate carbohydrates, low fat, and moderate protein provides sustained energy without gastrointestinal discomfort.

questions.question: Consuming protein prior to training (even during fasting periods) can help:
options: Preserve muscle mass and optimize performance
questions.answer_text: Preserve muscle mass and optimize performance
questions.explanation_en: Providing protein prior to training can help preserve muscle mass and optimize performance.

questions.question: Which grip type is typically used for a deadlift to enhance grip strength and prevent bar rotation?
questions.explanation_en: A mixed grip (one hand overhand, one underhand) increases bar security and helps prevent rotation during deadlifts.

questions.question: During a back squat, at what joint should the lifter initiate the movement first?
questions.explanation_en: Proper squat mechanics begin with the hips moving backward, keeping the weight over the midfoot and minimizing knee stress.

questions.question: Which cue is MOST appropriate to maintain proper form during a bench press?
options: Lift hips off the bench for more power
questions.explanation_en: Keeping the scapulae retracted and depressed provides shoulder stability and safer movement during the bench press.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the eccentric phase in a plyometric exercise?
questions.explanation_en: The eccentric phase occurs when the muscle lengthens under tension, such as during the landing phase of a jump.

questions.question: Which drill is most appropriate for developing lower-body power in an athlete?
questions.explanation_en: Bounding exercises develop explosive strength and elastic power in the lower body muscles.

questions.question: Refer to the diagram below of a depth jump setup. Which key aspect should be emphasized when performing a depth jump?
questions.explanation_en: Reducing ground contact time maximizes the explosive power transfer from eccentric to concentric contraction.

questions.question: What component of speed is most influenced by resistance sprint drills?
questions.explanation_en: Resistance sprint drills (like sled pushes) primarily improve the early acceleration phase of sprinting.

questions.question: Which drill best develops change-of-direction speed?
questions.explanation_en: The T-test involves forward sprinting, side shuffling, and backward running, improving multi-directional agility.

questions.question: Elite sprinters are characterized by:
questions.explanation_en: Elite sprinters minimize ground contact time, maximizing force application into the ground for speed development.

questions.question: In Olympic weightlifting, the second pull is characterized by:
options: First upward pull from the floor
questions.explanation_en: The second pull involves explosive extension at the hips, knees, and ankles to generate maximal bar acceleration.

questions.question: When coaching a volleyball athlete, which exercise is MOST sport-specific?
questions.explanation_en: Depth jumps closely mimic the explosive nature of vertical jumping in volleyball, making it sport-specific.

questions.question: Which muscle group is crucial for shoulder stabilization during overhead movements like pitching?
questions.explanation_en: Rotator cuff muscles stabilize the shoulder during high-velocity overhead motions like pitching.

questions.question: Dynamic stretching is recommended before activity because it:
questions.explanation_en: Dynamic stretching increases core temperature and mobility, preparing muscles for activity without compromising performance.

questions.question: Which flexibility exercise best improves hip extension mobility relevant to deep squats?
questions.explanation_en: Hip flexor stretches improve hip extension and mobility, essential for deep squats.

questions.question: Which tool is commonly used for self-myofascial release to reduce muscle tension and improve tissue quality?
questions.explanation_en: Foam rollers are commonly used for self-myofascial release to reduce muscle tension and improve tissue quality.

questions.question: Which analysis identifies the most common injuries in a sport to design preventive and corrective programs?
questions.explanation_en: Injury analysis identifies the most common injuries in a sport to design preventive and corrective training programs.

questions.question: In program design, beginners should first focus on:
questions.explanation_en: Beginners should focus on mastering basic movement patterns and correct technique before progressing to complex exercises.

questions.question: In linear periodization, training intensity typically:
questions.explanation_en: In linear periodization, intensity increases while training volume decreases progressively over time.

questions.question: Which phase of periodization emphasizes foundational strength, hypertrophy, and general fitness before sport-specific training?
questions.explanation_en: The preparatory phase emphasizes foundational strength, hypertrophy, and basic fitness before advancing to sport-specific training.

questions.question: A mesocycle typically lasts:
questions.explanation_en: A mesocycle typically spans 4–6 weeks and focuses on achieving specific adaptation like strength or endurance.

questions.question: Power or explosive exercises should typically be performed:
options: At the end of the workout when fatigued
Early in the workout when fresh
questions.answer_text: Early in the workout when fresh
questions.explanation_en: Power movements should be prioritized early in the workout when the athlete is not fatigued.

questions.question: The primary goal of hypertrophy training is to:
questions.explanation_en: Hypertrophy training aims to increase muscle size by promoting muscle fiber growth.

questions.question: Training at approximately 85% of 1RM for low repetitions typically targets:

questions.explanation_en: Training at ~85% of 1RM for low repetitions is characteristic of maximal strength development.

questions.question: Which lift is an example of a compound, multi-joint movement typically prioritized early in a session?
questions.explanation_en: Compound, multi-joint movements should be prioritized early in the session when the athlete is fresh.

questions.question: A training program that alternates upper and lower body exercises within the same session is designed to:
questions.explanation_en: Alternating upper and lower body exercises can improve training efficiency and recovery during the session.

questions.question: Circuit training most strongly emphasizes:
questions.explanation_en: Circuit training minimizes rest between exercises, promoting muscular endurance and aerobic conditioning.

questions.question: Supercompensation is most associated with the:

questions.question: A hallmark sign of overtraining is:
options: Decreased performance despite high training volume
questions.answer_text: Decreased performance despite high training volume
questions.explanation_en: Persistent performance decline along with fatigue are hallmark signs of overtraining.

questions.question: Most athletes require approximately how much sleep per night to support recovery and performance?
questions.explanation_en: Athletes require 7–9 hours of sleep per night to support recovery, hormone regulation, and overall performance.

questions.question: A recommended training space allocation per athlete in a weight room is approximately:
questions.explanation_en: Providing 35–50 square feet per athlete ensures safety, comfort, and freedom of movement during training sessions.

questions.question: An important factor in weight room design to reduce accidents and congestion is:
options: Safe flow of traffic and equipment accessibility
questions.answer_text: Safe flow of traffic and equipment accessibility
questions.explanation_en: Safety and efficiency in movement are critical factors in facility design to prevent accidents and congestion.

questions.question: A treadmill should be placed near exits primarily to:
options: Allow quick evacuation and reduce obstruction

questions.question: The legal responsibility of fitness professionals to take necessary actions to protect clients from harm is called:

questions.question: Keeping equipment safe and functional to reduce injury risk requires:
questions.explanation_en: Keeping equipment safe and functional significantly reduces the risk of injury during workouts.

questions.question: Which document, signed before participation, outlines the risks involved in physical activity?
questions.explanation_en: A liability waiver informs clients of potential risks and reduces legal exposure for fitness facilities.

questions.question: Which of the following actions by a coach would be considered unethical?
questions.explanation_en: Suggesting or providing banned substances is unethical and against professional conduct standards.

questions.question: Which law requires that individuals with disabilities have equal access to public facilities, including fitness centers?
questions.explanation_en: The ADA mandates that facilities must be accessible to individuals with disabilities.

questions.question: If a coach shares an athlete’s private health information without consent, they may be violating which law?
questions.explanation_en: HIPAA protects the confidentiality of medical records and personal health information.

questions.question: When purchasing new weight room equipment, what is the most important factor to consider?
questions.explanation_en: Equipment must meet safety and durability standards to ensure athlete safety and long-term use.

questions.question: Which piece of equipment requires the most frequent inspection due to heavy usage?
questions.explanation_en: These high-load equipment pieces are heavily used and critical for safety, requiring regular inspections.

questions.question: Which preventive maintenance step is essential for treadmills?
questions.explanation_en: Proper lubrication prevents friction, overheating, and premature wear on treadmill belts.

questions.question: Which of the following best promotes professional development among strength and conditioning staff?
options: Encouraging participation in continuing education courses
Offering bonuses only for high attendance
questions.answer_text: Encouraging participation in continuing education courses
questions.explanation_en: Continued education ensures that coaches stay current with the latest research and best practices.

questions.question: What is the MOST important factor when hiring new strength and conditioning staff?
questions.explanation_en: Credentials and hands-on experience are critical for ensuring qualified, safe, and effective coaching.

questions.question: In a staff evaluation process, which of the following should be emphasized the most?
options: Adherence to professional standards and job performance
Number of hours spent in the facility
questions.answer_text: Adherence to professional standards and job performance
questions.explanation_en: Evaluations should focus on professionalism, effectiveness, and the ability to uphold safety and ethical standards.

questions.question: Which of the following tests measures maximum muscular strength?
questions.explanation_en: The 1RM bench press measures maximal strength by determining the heaviest weight an individual can lift once.

questions.question: Which performance test would best assess lower-body explosive power?
questions.explanation_en: The standing long jump measures horizontal explosive power from the lower body.

questions.question: During strength testing, how much rest is recommended between maximal attempts?
questions.explanation_en: Sufficient recovery (2–5 minutes) between maximal attempts helps ensure accurate strength assessment.

questions.question: Which test is MOST appropriate for assessing aerobic endurance in well-trained athletes?
questions.explanation_en: The Cooper test evaluates aerobic endurance by measuring the distance covered in 12 minutes.

questions.question: Which of the following primarily assesses anaerobic capacity?
questions.explanation_en: The Wingate test measures peak anaerobic power and anaerobic capacity during a 30-second maximal effort cycle.

Which method provides the MOST accurate assessment of body fat percentage?
questions.explanation_en: Hydrostatic weighing is considered the gold standard for body composition measurement, despite being less accessible.

questions.question: Which skinfold site is measured for a three-site skinfold test for women?
questions.explanation_en: These are standard skinfold sites for estimating body fat percentage in women using the three-site method.

questions.question: When using a skinfold caliper, how long should you wait after pinching the skin before taking the measurement?
questions.explanation_en: Waiting 3 seconds after pinching allows the skinfold to stabilize, providing a more accurate measurement.

questions.question: Which movement screen assesses stability and mobility of the shoulders?
questions.explanation_en: The shoulder mobility test evaluates bilateral shoulder range of motion, combining internal rotation with adduction.

questions.question: During the deep squat test, a compensatory movement such as heel lift-off typically indicates tightness in which muscle group?
questions.explanation_en: Tight calves can restrict ankle dorsiflexion, causing heels to lift during a deep squat.

questions.question: Which functional movement screen best identifies asymmetries in single-leg strength and mobility?
questions.explanation_en: The hurdle step challenges single-leg balance, strength, and mobility, revealing side-to-side asymmetries.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of performance analysis in strength and conditioning programs?
options: To monitor progress and adjust programs accordingly
questions.answer_text: To monitor progress and adjust programs accordingly
questions.explanation_en: Performance analysis helps in evaluating effectiveness and making necessary modifications to training programs.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key performance indicator (KPI) for a sprinter?
questions.explanation_en: Sprint times like the 40-yard dash are primary indicators of speed performance for sprinters.

questions.question: In athlete performance testing, why is it important to test under similar conditions (same time of day, similar environment)?
options: To ensure consistency and validity of results
questions.answer_text: To ensure consistency and validity of results
questions.explanation_en: Testing under consistent conditions ensures that performance changes are due to training, not environmental factors.

questions.question: Which variable is MOST critical when assessing muscular power using the vertical jump test?
questions.explanation_en: Muscular power is a combination of strength and speed; in vertical jumps, quick force production is essential.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of conducting a 1RM test for the bench press?
questions.explanation_en: 1RM testing measures the maximal amount of force that can be exerted by the upper body muscles.

questions.question: The Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test is designed to assess an athlete’s:
questions.explanation_en: The Yo-Yo test evaluates an athlete’s ability to repeatedly perform intense exercise with short recovery periods.

questions.question: Which protocol is BEST for testing an athlete’s maximal aerobic capacity (VO2 max)?
questions.explanation_en: The Cooper test is widely used to estimate VO2 max based on the distance covered in 12 minutes of running.

questions.question: Which tool is primarily used in a skinfold measurement to assess body fat percentage?
questions.explanation_en: Skinfold calipers measure subcutaneous fat thickness at standard sites to estimate total body fat percentage.

questions.question: If an athlete’s weight remains constant but their body fat percentage decreases, this indicates an increase in:
questions.explanation_en: A drop in body fat percentage while maintaining weight typically indicates gains in lean muscle tissue.

questions.question: Which movement pattern is evaluated during the inline lunge test in FMS?
options: Lower body unilateral stability and mobility
questions.answer_text: Lower body unilateral stability and mobility
questions.explanation_en: The inline lunge test assesses balance, strength, and mobility on each leg individually.

questions.question: During the active straight leg raise test, what is the primary factor being assessed?
questions.explanation_en: The active straight leg raise measures the flexibility and control of the hamstrings and hip flexors.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes a qualitative analysis in sports performance testing?
options: Using force plates for jumping analysis
Observing movement patterns for technique evaluation
questions.answer_text: Observing movement patterns for technique evaluation
questions.explanation_en: Qualitative analysis involves subjective assessments such as evaluating an athlete’s movement efficiency and form.

questions.question: When analyzing performance test results, what is the primary benefit of using norm-referenced data?
options: Comparing an athlete to personal bests
Comparing an athlete’s performance to a larger reference group
questions.answer_text: Comparing an athlete’s performance to a larger reference group
questions.explanation_en: Norm-referenced data allows athletes to compare their performance against standard benchmarks from peer groups.

questions.question: Which structure primarily stores elastic energy during the stretch-shortening cycle?
questions.explanation_en: Elastic energy is stored primarily in the series elastic component (tendons and cross-bridge elasticity).

questions.question: Power is best defined as:

questions.question: Which muscle fiber type has the highest fatigue resistance?

questions.question: Which factor MOST influences acceleration?

questions.question: Torque is calculated as:

questions.question: Which adaptation occurs earliest with resistance training?
questions.explanation_en: Early strength gains are largely due to neural adaptations.

questions.question: Which training variable is MOST important for power?

questions.question: Which phase of periodization emphasizes hypertrophy and basic strength?

questions.question: Linear periodization typically involves:

questions.question: Which plyometric guideline MOST reduces injury risk?

questions.question: Which sprint drill BEST improves acceleration?

questions.question: Which exercise is closed-chain?

questions.question: A hallmark of overtraining syndrome is:
questions.explanation_en: Chronic fatigue and declining performance indicate overtraining.

questions.question: Which macronutrient provides the greatest energy per gram?
questions.explanation_en: Fat provides approximately 9 kcal per gram.

questions.question: Which nutrient timing strategy best supports glycogen resynthesis?
questions.explanation_en: Carbohydrates consumed soon after training accelerate glycogen restoration.

questions.question: Which supplement is legal and effective for short-duration high-intensity exercise?
questions.explanation_en: Creatine improves ATP-PCr availability and is legal.

questions.question: Dehydration exceeding ~2% body weight can impair:
